defects.defect: A gate level is dropped without a word. The roadmap's exit gates for mail and for web reading name observability levels as well as security ones (mail: S3 O3 E2; web: S2 O2 E2). The earlier wave definition recorded the trace and attribution levels O2 and O3 as 'not carried, because local models were skipped; only the 30-day retention on the readers' records is carried'. This proposal keeps the 30-day retention but never records O2 or O3 as not carried: not in wave A's list of departures, not in wave B's list of gate parts that are not built, not in its notes. Tony would sign waves A and B without seeing that line.

The daily Google sign-in check is moved to the first build step of wave B, although the approved S14 says it is 'added with mail'. Wave A is then signed off and left running with two scheduled 07:00 texts and nothing that tells Tony a sign-in has expired, so the first sign of it is a missing or empty morning text. The roadmap's own cadence (audit after every update and each month, quarterly restore drill and key rotation), which this card turns into Tony's calendar reminders, also arrives one wave late. The move is stated openly and is for size, but it weakens 'safe to leave running' for the first private-data wave.

Order inside the wave: saved notes (phase 2) come before the house-rules plugin exists and before T5 (phase 3). The notes fallback after a failed T6 is 'one house-rules rule on where notes may be written' and rests on T5's file-write turn, so on that branch the notes phase needs something the next phase builds. The same order also means the write tools are granted before T5 has shown that a blocking check is called for them.

The browser's coded rule is 'for the web helper, a short allowlist of read-only actions', but T5 here only checks that the blocking check is given the action name. It does not check that the check is told the helper's own id when the helper runs as a hand-off, which the rule needs to apply to the right agent. Wave B's four planted cases are also not said to be run again through the browser.

The wave that carries the roadmap's browser gate also adds two unattended host scripts outside the sandbox and the outbound proxy, one of which uses a parent's calendar sign-in with busy times shared across the two parents. That is three sub-kinds of new exposure in one plan. For the page watch, how the firewall treats the script's fetch is only 'checked and written down'; nothing holds the script to the one registered host and no log line is asked for.

Shared with the other two proposals. The video and podcast reader is a second program on the Mac that fetches public addresses outside the fetch tool's own check and outside the outbound proxy Tony asked for before web reading. It goes live on one check, 'the wrapper refuses a home-network address'. Wave B asks three things of the page-fetch path (an address typed in, one reached by a redirect, one reached by a name that resolves to it); the new fetcher is not asked the second and third.

Three thin spots in the gate before the send tool. (1) It is not written that the send tool is granted to no agent before the send-to-owner rule is live; the phase lists the mail-out server as 'allowed by name on each parent's own agent' ahead of T5 and the rule. (2) T5's send-tool turn checks the fields that can set a recipient but not that the check is told which agent is calling, which the rule 'the one recipient is the owner of the calling agent' depends on. (3) The injected web page is not said to be read through wave E's browser as well as the plain reader.

The shared list is the one way out whose audience is not held in code (Apple's sharing decides who sees it), and it lands on the agents that hold private data and read outside content. The wave has no planted test for it at all: no recipe page or file that asks for something to be added without a yes, and no eval-copy check that another list or a deletion is out of reach. The exit test only shows that it works.

For acting in the house the limits in code are in place before go-live, but the switching part has no planted-instruction test: only printing has one. Go-live checks the volume cap and nothing else; it does not show that a room left out cannot be switched or that no tool exists for a lock, garage, alarm or gate. Shared with the other two: the card gives the gateway's own process the macOS Local Network permission, and no proposal runs wave B's home-network refusals again afterwards.

The notes say the first paired device gets a plan of its own, but voice memos (two new programs on the Mac, and a path by which audio could reach the cloud model) are built in the same plan, first. Two kinds in one wave, each in its own phase. The Talk step leaves out the card's line that Talk's fallback agent is set to an agent with no memory.

The last wave adds the two highest kinds of risk in one plan with one exit test: a first paired device (Tony's phone) and screen control. The roadmap's rule is one new kind per plan where possible, and here it is possible: the deps proposal does it, and the split is clean after the deny list (about 10 hours for the phone, about 14 for the pilot by my count). As drawn, the deny list is deployed, the phone is paired, and days later in the same plan two entries of that Gateway-wide list are lifted for the pilot, with no signed-off stretch in which the phone alone has run. Each part does go live in its own phase after its own check, and step zero and the re-read of the phone's command list are kept.

The trace and attribution levels are recorded as not carried for mail in wave A, but the web gate's level (O2) is missing from wave B's own 'not carried' list and from the notes' list of roadmap lines no wave carries. A smaller version of the deps omission.

The printed stop-and-check sheet, Jordan's half page and test T8 leave wave A for wave B. Wave A then ends with two scheduled texts running before anything on paper says what each one is, how Tony switches it off, or what Happy's error line looks like. No roadmap gate is involved and the sign-in check, which matters more for leaving mail running, stays in A.

The reply check ('what did your last message say?', and Tony's signature if his own agent can quote the 07:00 text) sits in the lookup phase only. It is not in wave A's exit test, and wave B's helper does not look for that signature before it goes live, as the earlier definition had it. Size: by my count the wave is 25.25 hours and about 51 steps, a hair over the proposal's own 25 and 49; it is one plan only with Jordan's inbox as the piece that gives way, which wave B does have room for.

Same order problem as deps: saved notes (phase 2) come before the house-rules plugin (phase 3), while the notes fallback after a failed T6 needs a rule in that plugin. T5 here has turns for a connector tool and the scheduling tool but none for the file-write tools.

Shared with the other two proposals: the video and podcast reader, a second fetcher on the Mac outside the fetch tool's check and outside the outbound proxy, is tested against a typed home-network address only, not against a redirect to one or a name that resolves to one. This proposal is otherwise the strictest on this card (the tool's flags are confirmed on the installed version, page scripts stay off, wave B's four planted cases are run again through the browser).

Shared with the other two proposals: the card gives the gateway's own process the macOS Local Network permission for the lights and speakers, and wave B's three home-network refusals on the page-fetch path, and wave F's 'the browser cannot reach the home network', are not run again after that change.

Same as the risk proposal's last wave: a first paired device and screen control, the two highest kinds of risk, in one plan with one exit test, although they can be separated. The proposal's own note says the wave 'splits cleanly into two short plans' and still draws it as one. The Talk step also leaves out the card's line that Talk's fallback agent is set to an agent with no memory.

Ways to send out (wave E) go live before the remaining readers (wave F: the read-only browser, the video and podcast reader, the page watch). That puts the higher kind of risk ahead of the lower, and it means the roadmap's test 'an injected web page cannot change the email recipient' is passed while only the plain reader exists. When the browser arrives in wave F the mail-out tool is already on the parents' agents, yet wave F's browser gate and exit test do not run that recipient test again through the browser, and do not run wave B's four planted cases through it either. The send-to-owner rule is in code and does not depend on which reader the text came from, so this is a missing re-test, not an open door.

Photos and PDFs go live before the outbound gate and before the web helper, the reverse of the earlier definition Tony saw ('after the helper has passed its tests'). No roadmap gate is broken: the photo card needs only its own planted-file test, and a parent's agent with no hand-off to the web is the lower-risk state. But the state that matters (files, the mail lookup and the hand-off together) first exists when the helper is switched on, and there the re-send of the planted PDF and photo is listed as work, not as a condition in 'goes live when'. Only the exit test catches it.

By its own count the wave is 25.25 hours and 51 steps, over both round limits, and the paper sheet, Jordan's half page and T8 are moved out to make even that. What gives way then runs through four near-full waves: Jordan's inbox to B (25.5 hours), so the day out to C (25.75 hours), so the flyer dates to D (24.5 hours). There is no slack before wave E. Nothing here breaks a gate, but a wave that is over its plan is where checks get skipped.

The house-rules plugin is the first blocking plugin, and a fault in it stops every tool call. It is shown to fail closed on an eval-only copy, but there is no check after the real deploy that the family's Happy still answers a text and that both 07:00 mail texts still arrive, which the other two proposals have. (Running T5 and T7 first in this wave is, on the other hand, the best order of the three.)

The wave is described as one kind of risk, data the two parents share, but it also adds the first unattended host script outside the sandbox: the calendar clash check, which uses a parent's calendar sign-in and shares each parent's busy times with the other's account. It is the first no-model command job the jobs script creates, and T3's command-job part is not named there.

Voice memos (two new programs on the Mac and a path by which audio could reach the cloud model) are built in the plan that first acts in the house. Two kinds in one wave, each in its own phase after its own check. Shared with the other two: the gateway's own process gets the macOS Local Network permission here and the home-network refusals from waves B and F are not run again.

For the page watch, how the firewall treats the script's fetch 'is checked', with no rule or log line that holds the script to the one registered host. Shared with the other two: the video and podcast reader is tested against a typed home-network address only, not a redirect or a name that resolves to one.

graft.what: Split the last wave in two, as deps does with its H and I. First the paired phone: the device deny list, then the app on Tony's iPhone, then Talk as the experimental step, with its own exit test and sign-off. Then, alone in the last wave, the screen-control pilot. This removes the base's one major defect. Voice memos can stay in the base's wave F, or move beside the phone as in deps (Talk can use the built-in Mac voice either way); by my count the phone plan is about 10 hours without them and about 14 with them, and the pilot about 14.

In wave C, make 'try it first: T5 and T7' the first build phase, before any rule is written and before saved notes. Add deps's detail that T5 also has a turn for the file-write tools. Then the plugin, and the knowledge of what a blocking check is given, exist before the notes fallback could be needed. Keep the base's order after that: reminders and the scheduling tool last.

Record the trace and attribution levels O2 and O3 as not carried in wave B's get-ready list and in the notes' list of roadmap lines no wave carries, beside the secret egress proxy and the tripwire. The base records them for mail only.

Put the reply check into wave A's exit test (deps has it there too), with the rule that the wave closes only once Tony has signed it if his own agent can quote the 07:00 text; and make that signature a condition for the web helper going live in wave B.

The note that the printed sheet, Jordan's half page and T8 need nothing from wave A and may be done in A's eight-day wait if the first week runs ahead, while being counted in B. With deps's wording that the sheet says what the 07:00 text is and how Tony switches it off, this puts the stop sheet on paper by wave A's exit whenever time allows.

List under 'tony_provides' the decisions a failed test asks of him, in the wave where the test runs: his choice if the day-8 search fails, his yes or no on the one documented fix if T4 fails, his decision on one layer for the calendar if T5 shows the check is not called for connector tools, and what comes next if T7 fails.

The note that by the house wave the jobs script holds eight or more scheduled jobs, that S9 brings the comparing generator back at that point, and that no wave counts hours for it. Every job's target must keep coming from the family file, which is the roadmap's rule.
After the device deny list is deployed, check the calendar connectors as well as the mail connector and the helper's browser, since by then all three exist.

graft.from: none of the three (judge's additions; tests only, no new mechanism)
graft.what: Three checks all three proposals lack. (1) Before the video and podcast reader goes live, ask of its wrapper the same three things wave B asks of the page-fetch path: a home-network address typed in, one reached by a redirect, one reached by a name that resolves to it. (2) In the house wave, after the gateway's process is given the macOS Local Network permission, run wave B's three home-network refusals and the browser's home-network test again. (3) For the shared Reminders list, keep the base's eval-copy check (no other list, no delete) and add one planted page or file that asks for an item to be added without a yes.
